quotes.text: The first app is not a feature demo. It is a business interface. And that difference changes almost every decision that comes after it
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes a first Power App as a business interface rather than a showcase.

quotes.text: If the thinking is clean, low code helps us express it faster. If the thinking is weak, low code helps us spread that weakness faster too.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable warning that low code amplifies design quality in both directions.

quotes.text: Canvas is usually the stronger choice when experience design drives adoption. Model driven is usually the stronger choice when data relationships drive operational work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear rule of thumb for choosing between canvas and model-driven apps.

quotes.text: The app is not the source of truth. The app is the front door into the source of truth.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concisely separates the interface layer from Dataverse as the data foundation.

quotes.text: There is a big difference between overbuilt and future ready. Overbuilt means the solution carries behavior the business has not yet validated.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Useful distinction for scoping a first release without ignoring real complexity.

Why the app solves only half the problem

takeaways: A first Power App should be a narrow business interface that makes one repeated request, such as a vacation request, enter a governed path with a visible status.
Choose canvas for a low-friction employee front door and model-driven apps where roles need oversight across many Dataverse records and relationships.
Keep release one small: avoid the default environment for operational apps, avoid unnecessary custom or premium connectors, and model future complexity like delegation in Dataverse first.
hook: Many first Power Platform projects stall because teams build screens before defining the process they want to change. Using a Contoso vacation request example, this episode shows makers and IT leads how to turn Dataverse tables into a working canvas front door, choose between canvas and model-driven apps, and avoid environment and licensing traps.
